blocks.text: ICM7555 General Purpose CMOS Timer DIP

The ICM7555 is a low-power CMOS implementation of the industry-standard 555 timer in a compact DIP-8 package. It is designed to produce accurate time delays and stable oscillations using only a few external components. Compared with bipolar 555 devices, the ICM7555 significantly reduces quiescent current and power-spike behavior during output transitions, making it a better fit for battery-powered and low-power instrumentation.

In operation the chip can be configured as either a monostable (one-shot) or astable (oscillator) timer; a single resistor–capacitor pair controls timing in monostable mode, while two resistors plus a capacitor set frequency and duty cycle in astable mode. The device provides TTL/CMOS-compatible output levels at 5 V and maintains stable timing characteristics across its recommended supply range, simplifying integration into mixed-logic systems.

Mechanically offered in DIP-8, SOP-8, MSOP-8 and DFN-8 packages, the ICM7555 balances compact footprint with straightforward through-hole or surface-mount assembly. Its low leakage on trigger/threshold/reset pins, modest thermal ratings and predictable switching times make it useful for a wide range of control and timing tasks where low standby current and stable timing are important.

blocks.text: The CD4017BE is a Decade Counter IC (also known as a Johnson Counter) with 10 decoded outputs. It is part of the CD4000 series of CMOS logic ICs and is designed for counting and sequencing applications.

blocks.v: Output pins Q0 to Q9 · These are the 10 output pins on which the counting occurs, they are not in order hence verify the pin diagram above
Vss or Ground · Connected to the Ground of the circuit
Carry Out (CO) · This pin goes high after the IC counts from 1 to 10. This is used as a carry while counting.
Clock Enable (EN) · This is an input that when made high will hold the count at the current state
Clock · The counting happens when this clock pulse goes high, this pin is normally connected to a 555 timer or other uC to produce a pulse
Resets · As the name suggests this pin resets the count back to 1
Vdd / Vcc · Connects to the supply voltage typically +5V

blocks.text: Note: Complete Technical Details can be found in the CD4017 datasheet given at the end of this page.

The IC CD4017 is used for counting applications, it has the capability to turn on 10 outputs sequentially in a pre-defined time and reset the count or hold it when required. It also has the capability to indicate the status of counting using Carry pin.
This is commonly used for Led chasers and other logical output projects, so if you are looking for a sequential decoded counting IC that can count up to 10 then this IC will be your right choice
How to use a CD4017 IC

The IC can work from 3V to 15V, but is normally powered with +5V to the Vdd/Vcc pin, and the Ground/Vss pin is connected to the ground. We have 10 output pins ranging from Q0 to Q9, these pins can be connected to any load but we are using LEDs here as shown in the circuit below.

This IC will increment the count from 0 to 9 (Q0 to Q9) each time it senses a high pulse from the clock pin (pin 14). So we need a clock source to keep this IC ticking, this clock source can be a simple Timer circuit that could generate pulse or a microcontroller like Arduino, PIC, etc. to generate our custom pulse using I/O pins.

The output changes sequentially from Q0 to Q9 for every high pulse from the Clock pin, but this sequence can be interrupted by two pins. They are the Clock Enable (pin 13) and Reset (pin 15) pins. These pins are held low (0V/grounded) by default, but when the Clock Enable pin is made high the counting pauses.

For example if the count was at pin Q3 when the Clock enable pin was made high, then the count will pause at pin Q3 irrespective of any high pulses from clock and will continue incrementing only when Clock Enable is made low again. Similarly, if the reset pin is made high. The count will reset itself back to Q0 and will stay there until Q0 is made low again.

We have another pin called the carry out pin (12th pin), this pin will stay low (0V) by default. But when the IC completes counting up to 10, the pin will go high and will remain high till it counts till 5, when its 5 it will go down (0V) and turn on again when it reaches 10. The R307 is a compact, self-contained optical fingerprint identification module that integrates an image sensor, on-board processing and flash storage so fingerprint capture, template generation and matching are handled inside the module. On power up the module initializes its sensor and firmware (≈200 ms) and then waits for commands over its serial or USB interface; when a finger is presented the unit acquires a greyscale image and stores it in the image buffer for processing.

Enrollment and verification workflows are implemented in the module: the host commands the R307 to capture images, convert them to character files, combine files into templates and store templates in the internal fingerprint library. The module supports both 1:1 verification and 1:N search modes and performs template matching internally, returning match results and scores to the host.

Despite its small physical footprint, the R307 exposes a rich instruction set (enroll, search, upload/download image/template, configure parameters, etc.), configurable system parameters (baud, security level, packet length) and a persistent flash library for templates — making it well suited for embedded access control, attendance and biometric projects where the host can be a microcontroller or a PC.

makers-483413.summary: 74123 A dual, retrigger able one-shot multivibrator IC in a 16-pin DIP. Generates precise output pulses with a width set by external RC components.

blocks.text: 74123 Dual Retrigger able Monostable Multivibrator With Clear DIP-16 IC

The 74123 is a monolithic integrated circuit that contains two independent retrigger able monostable multivibrators in a single DIP-16 package. A monostable multivibrator, also known as a “one-shot,” is a circuit that produces a single output pulse of a predetermined duration each time it is triggered by an external signal. This chip is designed to generate precise, timed intervals from transient input signals.

The device offers significant flexibility in how it is triggered and controlled. Each multivibrator features both active-low (A) and active-high (B) trigger inputs, allowing it to be initiated by either a rising or falling edge from gated logic signals. A key characteristic is its retrigger able capability, which allows the output pulse to be extended by applying a new trigger before the initial timing period expires. Furthermore, an overriding Clear input provides immediate termination of the output pulse.

The duration of the output pulse is not fixed internally but is programmed by connecting external timing components a resistor (R_T) and a capacitor (C_ext). This allows the pulse width to be tailored from nanoseconds to seconds, making the chip highly versatile. The output is provided in both true (Q) and complementary (Q̅) forms, offering additional logic flexibility for system design.

blocks.text: The TL7702 is a compact, integrated supply-voltage supervisor provided in a standard DIP-8 package. Designed for system reset control, it monitors a designated sense input and produces defined reset outputs during power-up and undervoltage events. The device integrates a temperature-compensated reference and an internal timer which, together with an external timing capacitor, determine the duration of reset assertion to ensure clean initialization of downstream logic.

In operation the TL7702 maintains the reset outputs active until monitored voltages exceed a precise threshold, then uses the timing capacitor to provide a controlled release. The device offers complementary reset outputs (active high and active low) with open-collector/open-drain style behavior that requires external pull-ups for logic-level signaling. Its compact DIP form factor simplifies prototyping and replacement in through-hole designs. It is tolerant of moderate supply transients too.

Engineers value the TL7702 for its predictable reset timing and the ability to adjust threshold behavior using a simple resistor divider at the SENSE pin. Built-in hysteresis and low reference drift across temperature reduce false triggers. The part’s documented thermal and ESD limits support safe board-level integration when layout guidance is followed, making it a straightforward choice for reliable system initialization in many designs.

باور بانك هيريجو اتش ار ٠٠٨ هو شاحن متنقل عملي بسعة ١٠٠٠٠ ملي أمبير، مناسب للاستخدام اليومي وللأشخاص الذين يحتاجون باور بانك خفيف وسهل الحمل مع دعم الشحن السريع. يتميز المنتج بوجود كابل تايب سي مدمج وكابل لايتنينج مدمج، مما يقلل الحاجة لحمل كابلات منفصلة عند شحن الموبايل أو الإكسسوارات المتوافقة.

هذا الموديل مناسب لمن يريد باور بانك أصغر من الإصدارات ذات السعة الأعلى، مع الحفاظ على أداء عملي وسرعة شحن جيدة للأجهزة المتوافقة. السعة ١٠٠٠٠ ملي أمبير مناسبة للاستخدام اليومي، سواء في الشغل أو الدراسة أو أثناء التنقل، كما أن الشاشة الرقمية الموجودة في الواجهة تساعدك على معرفة نسبة الشحن المتبقية بشكل واضح قبل الخروج أو أثناء الاستخدام.

طبقًا للصور والبيانات المرسلة، يأتي موديل هيريجو اتش ار ٠٠٨ بدعم شحن سريع حتى ٢٢.٥ وات، مع خرج من كابل تايب سي مدمج يصل إلى ١٠ فولت و٢.٢٥ أمبير، وخرج من كابل لايتنينج بقيمة ٥ فولت و٢.٤ أمبير. كما تعرض الصور أمثلة تقريبية لعدد مرات الشحن، مثل حوالي ٢.٥ شحنة لبعض موديلات آيفون، وحوالي شحنتين لبعض موبايلات سامسونج، وحوالي شحنة واحدة لبعض أجهزة التابلت، وعدد كبير من الشحنات للسماعات اللاسلكية الصغيرة. العدد الفعلي يختلف حسب سعة بطارية الجهاز وحالتها وطريقة الاستخدام.
